facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

support_spans: A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
concepts.why: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells and uniform positivity for CD207/langerin supports the diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The patient's history of myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts, along with the presence of a skin lesion, suggests the possibility of myelodysplastic syndrome-associated skin infiltration.

support_spans: BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
concepts.why: The identification of BRAF-V600E variant status through immunohistochemical studies suggests the possibility of a BRAF-V600E mutant melanocytic neoplasm.
The patient's history of myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts, along with the presence of a skin lesion, suggests the possibility of leukemia cutis.
The negative myeloperoxidase staining in the skin biopsy specimen points towards indeterminate cell histiocytosis.

rationales.F05: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F06: Uniform positivity for CD207/langerin is a characteristic feature of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F08: The presence of the BRAF-V600E variant is more commonly associated with BRAF-V600E mutant melanocytic neoplasm.
